introduction.headline: A generated prior life rooted in Cần Thơ
introduction.summary: Viewer-validation fixture for an unpublished Genesis candidate: ten historical episodes, six autobiographical memories, and remembered meanings remain distinct. This is not a born or live Thread.

origins.title: What this candidate began with
origins.summary: De novo symbolic genome input, not mature character: gathers concrete examples before challenging broad claims; persists when others rely on the outcome; protects concentration; checks quieter participants; repairs useful objects; revisits decisions when evidence changes tradeoffs.

places.summary: Mid-rise home on a mixed residential-commercial street with small shops, courtyards, pedestrians, and motorbikes.
Vietnamese public neighborhood school with classrooms, science and arts facilities, a schoolyard, and after-school activities.
Local bus and river connections where heat, rain, traffic, and changing schedules affect ordinary travel.
Public library with Vietnamese collections, newspapers, study tables, computers, and some English-language or translated material.
Market and nearby commercial streets with groceries, prepared food, household goods, repairs, and small independent businesses.

relationships.summary: Lives in the household and appears across errands, spending choices, supervision, and growing independence.
Lives in the household and is four years younger; appears across play and repeated household-choice episodes.
Lives in the subject household in Cần Thơ.
Lives elsewhere in Cần Thơ and sometimes helps with childcare or transport.

timeline.title: Clearing the floor
timeline.summary: Helps clear plastic animals into a blue basket so the floor can be swept; the younger sibling contributes one toy.

timeline.title: The red toy truck
timeline.summary: A tug over a red toy truck ends when the caregiver asks both children to stop pulling and take turns; the subject lets go first.

timeline.title: The missing pencil case
timeline.summary: A missing blue pencil case is found wedged in the sofa after the younger sibling points toward it.

timeline.title: Tomatoes and change
timeline.summary: Sent alone to the next market row with 20,000 đồng to buy half a kilo of tomatoes, check the price, and return with the change.

timeline.title: Blue or red sandals
timeline.summary: Compares blue and red sandals for the younger sibling, explains comfort versus appearance, then leaves the choice to the sibling, who picks red.

timeline.title: Soap instead of snacks
timeline.summary: With little cash and almost no dish soap, argues for buying soap instead of snacks and explains the household tradeoff.

timeline.title: Soap and rice at the market
timeline.summary: Goes alone through the market with money and a list to buy dish soap and two kilos of rice, then returns with the items and remaining change.

timeline.title: Oil, snacks, and a drawing
timeline.summary: Uses a notebook and simple drawing to explain cooking oil versus snacks, then leaves the final choice to the younger sibling, who chooses oil.

timeline.title: Rice or snacks
timeline.summary: Writes two price columns to compare a full sack of rice with less rice plus snacks; the siblings agree on the full sack.

timeline.title: English class or drawing course
timeline.summary: Reads a school notice and chooses an extra English class over the younger sibling's planned drawing course; the sibling remains silent.

memories.title: Tomatoes and change
memories.rememberedContent: Being sent alone in the crowded market with 20,000 đồng to buy tomatoes, watching them weighed and bagged, then returning the tomatoes and change to the waiting adults.

memories.title: Blue or red sandals
memories.rememberedContent: Helping the younger sibling compare blue and red sandals, explaining the practical and aesthetic difference, then watching the sibling choose red.

memories.title: Soap instead of snacks
memories.rememberedContent: A low-cash afternoon when the caregiver asked for a choice between snacks and dish soap; after checking the nearly empty bottle, the subject argued for soap.
uncertainty: Whether everyone was sitting or standing

memories.title: Soap and rice at the market
memories.rememberedContent: Going alone through the neighborhood market with money and a short list, buying dish soap and two kilos of rice, then returning with the purchases and remaining money.

memories.title: Oil, snacks, and a drawing
memories.rememberedContent: A humid morning when only cooking oil or snacks could be bought; the subject used a notebook drawing to explain the tradeoff and the younger sibling chose oil.

memories.title: Rice, English, and drawing
memories.rememberedContent: Remembering two resource choices: writing price columns for rice versus snacks, and later choosing an extra English class instead of the younger sibling's drawing course.
uncertainty: Exact words around the rice choice
How long the later hesitation lasted

meanings.title: Tomatoes and change
meanings.summary: The tomato errand now carries a stronger sense of practical responsibility: small-money competence becomes connected to later household resource choices that can affect other family members.

meanings.title: Blue or red sandals
meanings.summary: The sandal choice now sits beside later tradeoffs: helping can respect another person's preference in small choices while practicality and adult expectations may still override quieter wishes in larger ones.

meanings.title: Soap instead of snacks
meanings.summary: A scarcity decision becomes associated with practical household responsibility and speaking up for what seems necessary.

meanings.title: Soap and rice at the market
meanings.summary: A modestly independent errand becomes a felt step toward being trusted and capable while handling money and household responsibility.

meanings.title: Oil, snacks, and a drawing
meanings.summary: The memory centers on making a constrained household choice gentler and more understandable for the younger sibling rather than on scarcity alone.

meanings.title: Rice, English, and drawing
meanings.summary: Limited-resource choices become associated with a practical explaining role and a tendency to favor longer-term usefulness over short-term preference.
